newsitem.title: ISRAEL: British tourist says "miracle" to survive shooting.
newsitem.headline: British tourist says "miracle" to survive shooting.

text.p: A British hitchhiker shot at close range in Israel's southern desert on Wednesday by a motorist who gave her a ride said a "miracle" kept her alive.
"I'm fine...a big miracle," Charlotte Gibb, 20, told Israel radio on Thursday.
Gibb's 22-year-old boyfriend, a British law student, was killed in the attack.
The British consulate in Tel Aviv named the dead man as Jeffrey Max Hunter, a law student from Surrey south of London.

Police said the two tourists had hitched a ride at a petrol station in the Red Sea resort of Eilat. The driver shot them during a stop 120 km (80 miles) north of the resort at about 1 a.m. (2200 GMT) and drove off.
"We were having a cigarette outside the car, during a rest from the journey, and then I just saw lots of flashes and he'd shot us," Gibb told reporters.
"There was silence, we weren't really speaking, and then I just saw the light," said Gibb, a student from Peterborough in eastern England.
Minutes after the shooting, soldiers found Gibb beside the road and administered first aid. The man died instantly.
Gibb spent Thursday recuperating in Soroka hospital in the town of Beersheba, where doctors carried out surgery on bullet wounds to her cheek, right hand and left arm.
British consular officials said she could be released as early as Sunday. Gibb's parents arrived in Israel on Thursday.
"They just wanted to make sure I was okay and they wanted not to worry, not to bother me and question me," Gibb told the radio.
The motive for the shooting, the second attack involving young British tourists in Israel in three weeks, was unclear.
Gibb told reporters that the driver spoke Hebrew but that she did not know whether he was an Israeli Jew or Arab.
Police said the driver may have fled to Egypt.
